subject.title: fix(agents): terminate mixed tool-call batches on critical loop veto

question: After a critical tool-loop veto ends the active run, should queued steering and follow-up messages be cancelled, or preserved for a new clean run?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes session-state behavior at a safety boundary, and source inspection cannot determine the desired user-visible recovery policy without runtime-owner intent.

options.title: Preserve for a fresh run
options.body: Terminate the degenerate run, then retain or explicitly requeue pending user input for processing by a clean subsequent run.

options.title: Cancel queued input
options.body: Terminate immediately and discard pending steering and follow-up messages, documenting that users must resend after the safety stop.

recommendation.title: Preserve for a fresh run
recommendation.body: Terminate the degenerate run, then retain or explicitly requeue pending user input for processing by a clean subsequent run.

likelyOwner.reason: The history connects this person to both configurable loop detection and the embedded runtime boundary where the policy must be implemented.
